identity.name: Polysorbate 65 (polyoxyethylene (20) sorbitan tristearate)
identity.chemical_class: Non-ionic polyoxyethylene sorbitan fatty acid ester emulsifier

function.mechanism: Acts as a non-ionic surfactant, lowering oil-water interfacial tension and stabilizing dispersed fat/water systems.
common_food_categories: frozen desserts (ice cream, ice milk, sherbet)

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI for E432-E436 from EFSA re-evaluation; reproductive toxicity database considered incomplete.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no concern for genotoxicity and no concern from chronic/carcinogenicity or developmental toxicity data, but set a temporary group ADI due to reproductive-toxicity data limitations.

adi.basis: ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw as total polyoxyethylene (20) sorbitan esters.

concerns.summary: Recent studies on related emulsifiers (especially polysorbate 80, not E436-specific) report microbiome composition shifts and epithelial/barrier effects; direct evidence for polysorbate 65 remains sparse.
EFSA identified an incomplete reproductive-toxicity dataset for polysorbates and therefore set a temporary group ADI with added uncertainty.

no_concern_confirmed: No EFSA concern for genotoxicity in the re-evaluation dataset.
No EFSA concern from chronic/carcinogenicity and developmental toxicity datasets.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA high-consumption estimates in toddlers were around the temporary group ADI (~10 mg/kg bw/day).

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approvals remain in place, but EFSA's temporary ADI, child high-end exposure proximity to ADI, and class-based mechanistic concerns from related emulsifiers support a moderate tier rather than limited/risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA temporary group ADI of 10 mg/kg bw/day
Direct E436-specific recent toxicology data are limited
Class evidence from related emulsifiers suggests potential gut barrier/microbiome effects
